standard.title: First Nations Australian music
standard.description: explore examples of music composed and/or performed by First Nations Australians
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored how arts are important for communities (AC9AMUFE01) including listening to First Nations Australians talk about arts and Country/Place. They have explored music from diverse cultural contexts (AC9AMU2E01). This is their first focused exploration of music specifically by First Nations Australian composers and performers.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore examples of music composed and/or performed by First Nations Australians across diverse styles, asking questions about instruments, voices, cultural messages and connections to Country/Place.

nodes.label: Where First Nations Australian music is heard
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify at least two contexts in which they can experience music composed or performed by First Nations Australians.
nodes.minimum_width: Name at least two contexts where they could hear First Nations Australian music (e.g. mainstream streaming, school ceremony, local festival, television).
nodes.typical_width: Identify and explore multiple contexts — mainstream music platforms, live performance, music for school or community ceremonies, state and national events, local festivals, choirs and orchestras, Welcome to Country and cultural openings.
wider: Access First Nations Australian music through different platform types (streaming service, live performance or community event, television) and compare how each context shapes the listening experience
Identify a local First Nations Australian musician or group and find out where their music can be experienced

response_modes.reason: Students often assume First Nations Australian music is only encountered in ceremonial or historical contexts. Broadening awareness to include mainstream media, contemporary performance and everyday community life challenges this assumption and opens up ongoing engagement.

success_criteria: Can name at least two contexts where First Nations Australian music can be experienced
Can identify at least one First Nations Australian musician, group or musical context they have encountered

nodes.label: Listening to diverse First Nations Australian music styles
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can listen to examples of First Nations Australian music across diverse styles and identify instruments, voices and features of the music.
nodes.minimum_width: Listen to at least one example of First Nations Australian music; identify one instrument or voice and describe one feature of the music.
nodes.typical_width: Listen to First Nations Australian music across diverse styles (mainstream media, local festival, choir/orchestra, ceremonial); identify instruments and voices; ask questions such as 'What instruments can I hear?', 'How is this music similar or different to other music I listen to?', 'How is this music communicating a message about Country/Place?'
wider: Compare two examples of First Nations Australian music from different styles or contexts — describe what is similar and what is different in the instruments, voices and feeling of each
Focus on one example and listen multiple times for different things — first for instruments, then for mood, then for what message the music might be communicating
nodes.hinge_reason: The quality of listening engagement here determines whether students engage with First Nations Australian music as genuine music-making or as cultural background. If students do not develop attentive, observational listening skills in this standard, they cannot access the more analytical exploration of cultural knowledge and connection to Country/Place in AC9AMU4E02.

response_modes.reason: Use explicit listening frames before and after each listening experience: 'We're going to listen for instruments first — put up your hand when you hear something you recognise.' After listening: 'What did you hear? What was surprising? What questions do you have?' Build observation habits rather than passive reception.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The diversity of First Nations Australian music styles is genuinely surprising to most students — encountering music from different regions, genres and purposes challenges assumptions and builds genuine curiosity. This diversity is a pedagogical asset.
success_criteria: Can identify at least one instrument or voice in a First Nations Australian music example
Can describe at least one feature of the music (e.g. tempo, mood, instrumentation) and ask at least one question about it

nodes.label: Music communicating messages about Country/Place
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explore how First Nations Australian music communicates messages about Country/Place, asking questions about how musical elements are used to carry those messages.
nodes.minimum_width: Listen to one piece of First Nations Australian music connected to Country/Place; identify one way the music might be communicating a message or feeling about a place.
nodes.typical_width: Explore screen-based or theatrical works that communicate First Nations Australian cultural knowledge — view animations or cartoons retelling traditional stories; use questions to explore how texture, melody, tempo and dynamics are used to represent characters, mood and narrative; ask 'How is this music telling me about this story/place?'
wider: Watch an animation or cartoon that retells a First Nations Australian story and focus on how the music changes when the setting or character changes — map the musical choices to the narrative
Use Viewpoints questions to analyse how specific elements of music (texture, tempo, dynamics, melody) are used to communicate specific aspects of a First Nations Australian story or place

response_modes.reason: The connection between music and cultural message is not self-evident to Y1-2 students. Guided Viewpoints questioning ('How is the music telling you about this character/place/moment?') builds the analytical framework that underpins deeper engagement with First Nations Australian cultural knowledge through music in subsequent bands.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Screen-based works that use First Nations Australian music to communicate cultural knowledge offer a rich bridge between music listening skills and cultural understanding — the analytical questions apply specifically to the music's role in storytelling, not just to the story itself.
success_criteria: Can identify how at least one element of music (e.g. tempo, dynamics) is being used in a First Nations Australian piece to create a specific effect
Can ask or respond to a question about how the music communicates a message or feeling about Country/Place
